tasks.short: Observe animals' appearance and behaviour, write observations on cage cards and sheets, type them into the animal database, and update breeding and genealogy records.

steps.what: Veterinary assistant observes animals' appearance, behaviour and feeding
Veterinary assistant records information on appearance, behaviour and feeding: on cage cards and paper sheets today, on a tablet at the cage after the change
Veterinary assistant types the sheets into the animal database
Veterinary assistant records genealogy and breeding information for pairings and litters

tasks.design: Observations are entered on a tablet at the cage by scanning its barcode in the animal management system ({OPS_SYSTEM}), with pick lists for common signs and a free note, so cage cards and sheets are not written and typed in later. New litters are registered at the breeding cage, which fills the parents and line from the cage record, so genealogy is not entered by hand. Observing animals stays with the assistant.
tasks.previous_blocker: Observations were written on paper and typed in at the end of the day.
tasks.enabler_now: Animal management systems take entries at the cage by barcode.
tasks.still_hard: Unusual behaviour does not fit a pick list.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that an animal is in pain before it shows clear signs.
tasks.altitude: The assistant observes instead of copying sheets.

evidence.claim: Animal management systems can take observations at the cage by barcode and link litters to their parents.
Licensed animal facilities must keep records of each animal's origin, use and fate under national rules.

assumptions: Boundary: from the animal round to breeding recorded; study design is outside.
Input contract: cages barcoded and tablets on the floor; fallback is paper sheets.

Entering on a tablet removes typing the sheets in later (s3); writing each observation stays, so s2 keeps 90 for the pick lists and notes. s4 keeps 50 because parents and line fill from the cage record and the assistant still records each litter.

incremental.description: Veterinary assistant corrects entries made at the wrong cage.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: tablets are shared and many cages lack barcodes, so half of sheets are still typed in and s3 keeps 50 (17.0); high: barcoded cages and tablets on the floor (24.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Listen to the client and look at the animal, advise on care, nutrition or behaviour, give written care instructions, and answer follow-up calls.

steps.what: Veterinary assistant listens to the client's question and looks at the animal
Veterinary assistant educates or advises clients on animal health care, nutrition or behaviour
Veterinary assistant writes care instructions for the client
Veterinary assistant answers clients' follow-up questions by phone

tasks.design: Standard care sheets per topic, such as diet change, dental care or house training, are kept in the practice system ({OPS_SYSTEM}) and printed with the pet's name and the advised amounts, so instructions are not written by hand each time. Listening, advising and answering calls stay with the assistant.
tasks.previous_blocker: Care instructions were written by hand for each client.
tasks.enabler_now: Practice systems print standard sheets filled with the pet's details.
tasks.still_hard: Unusual cases need written advice from the vet.
tasks.human_edge: Getting a worried owner to follow a diet plan.

evidence.claim: Practice systems can print standard care sheets filled with the animal's details.

assumptions: Boundary: from the client question to questions answered; diagnosis by the vet is outside.
Input contract: care sheets approved by the vets; fallback is handwriting.
Advising does not change. s3 keeps 50 because the sheet gives the standard text, and the assistant still enters the amounts and writes what is particular to the pet.

incremental.description: Veterinary assistant keeps care sheets current with the vets.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: mostly unusual questions the sheets do not cover, so s3 keeps 85 (1.7); high: many routine diet and care questions (7.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Collect study data from cage sheets and instruments, enter it, write the report section, check it, send it to the researcher, and file forms.

steps.what: Veterinary assistant collects study data from cage sheets, scales and instruments
Veterinary assistant maintains research information in the study spreadsheet
Veterinary assistant writes the report section for the study
Veterinary assistant checks the final report section: tables and graphs against the study data, the narrative against what was observed, and the researcher it goes to
Veterinary assistant sends the checked report section to the researcher: by e-mail today, by one release from the system after the change
Veterinary assistant performs clerical duties by filing study forms and certificates in binders

tasks.design: Observations come from the animal management system ({OPS_SYSTEM}) and weights from scales linked to it, so study data are not collected from sheets and typed into a spreadsheet; the assistant checks and adds the few manual values. A report template fills tables and graphs per study from the data, and the assistant writes the short narrative. The assistant checks the report section and releases it once to the researcher from the system. Study forms and certificates are filed digitally by study number in the document system ({DOCS}) instead of binders.
tasks.previous_blocker: Data were collected from paper and typed; reports and binders were assembled by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Linked scales and animal systems feed study data and report templates.
tasks.still_hard: Some instruments have no data link.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that a weight that is in range is still wrong for that animal.
tasks.altitude: The assistant checks data instead of typing them.

evidence.claim: Lab scales and animal management systems can be linked so weights go straight into study records.
Studies under good laboratory practice rules need an audit trail of raw data.

assumptions: Boundary: from the study period to forms filed; study analysis is outside.
Input contract: scales linked and studies set up; fallback is paper and spreadsheets.
The assistant checks every report section; s5 keeps 20 for the release.

incremental.description: Veterinary assistant enters values from instruments without data links.

approvals.approved_version: The report section with tables, graphs and narrative exactly as checked by the assistant in s4, sent once to the study's researcher; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many manual instruments without links, so s1 keeps 70 and s2 keeps 60 (42.5); high: linked scales and routine studies (60.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Enter treatments and products for billing, take payments, check unpaid invoices, send reminders, count stock, and enter daily takings in the books.

steps.what: Veterinary assistant bills customers by entering treatments and products used
Veterinary assistant takes payment at the desk
Veterinary assistant checks the reminder list: each client, invoice and amount, that it is still unpaid, and the e-mail address
Veterinary assistant sends payment reminders to clients: e-mailed one by one today, by one release from the system after the change
Veterinary assistant maintains inventories by counting medicines and food on the shelves
Veterinary assistant does bookkeeping by entering daily takings in the books: all takings today, only cash takings after the change
Veterinary assistant checks the day's bookings before posting: card and invoice totals against the terminal and the day's invoices, and the accounts
Veterinary assistant posts the checked takings to the bookkeeping

tasks.design: Treatments and products recorded in the patient record of the practice system ({OPS_SYSTEM}) become invoice lines, so the assistant checks the invoice instead of entering each item. The system lists unpaid invoices past their due date; the assistant checks the list and releases the reminders once by e-mail from the system. Products sold or used are booked out of stock, so counts become spot checks, and payments from the card terminal and invoices come into the bookkeeping ({ERP}) as proposed bookings; the assistant adds cash, checks the day's bookings and posts them once. Taking payment stays with the assistant.
tasks.previous_blocker: Items were entered by hand, reminders typed and takings copied into the books.
tasks.enabler_now: Practice systems link records, invoices, stock and bookkeeping.
tasks.still_hard: Clients who dispute a bill need a conversation.
tasks.human_edge: Handling a bill with an owner whose pet has just died.
tasks.altitude: The assistant checks invoices instead of typing them.

reach.learn: Whether income and stock are current.

evidence.claim: Veterinary practice systems can turn recorded treatments into invoice lines and book products out of stock.
Invoices and bookkeeping records must be kept for several years under national tax rules.

assumptions: Boundary: from the visit finished to takings booked; annual accounts are outside.

Input contract: price list and stock set up in the practice system; products and medicines booked out through the invoice lines and treatments the vet records (s1); supplier deliveries booked in by the assistant on arrival; fallback is entering by hand.
The assistant checks the reminder list every time; s4 keeps 10 for the release. s6 keeps 15 for cash takings; the takings check and the posting keep their full time.
The vet records treatments in the record as before.
Coverage: medicines used in treatments are not always recorded, so counts become spot checks mainly for food and retail stock; s5 keeps 60%.

incremental.description: Veterinary assistant corrects stock after spot counts.
Veterinary assistant books supplier deliveries into stock on arrival.

approvals.approved_version: The reminders for the clients, invoices and amounts exactly as checked by the assistant in s3, sent once by e-mail to each client's address in the practice system; any change needs a new check.
The day's takings bookings with card, invoice and cash totals exactly as checked by the assistant in s6b, posted once to the practice's bookkeeping; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a small practice with few products and many treatments not recorded in time, so s1 keeps 60 and s5 keeps 90 (30.5); high: a busy practice with a shop (43.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The veterinary assistant keeps observing animals, advising clients, checking data and taking payments; paper sheets, typed data, handwritten instructions and copied takings shrink.
role.ambitious_version: An assistant with more time with the animals.

job.title: Veterinary Assistants and Laboratory Animal Caretakers
